title: The Big Beat (1957) and using Barnet's band for the whole picture
summary: Barnet accompanied the Mills Brothers in The Big Beat and Will Cowan then used his band for the rest of the film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Somebody who shouldn't be loose. Okay. You didn't play soprano sax. Al was the featured soloist on --
"Andy's Boogie."
On "Andy's Boogie."
A very short movie, three minutes.
Right. What did you play? Which horn were you playing?
I think I played alto on that, on that --
Okay. The next listing in here, in your films, is, "The Big Beat," 82 minutes, 1957, Director, Will
Cowan.
A biggie.

A series of musical numbers loosely strung together with a skimpy plot, interesting only for appearances by Charlie Barnet, Buddy Bregman, Harry James, George Shearing and his Quintet, (Percy Bryce, drums), and the Cal Tjader Quintet, Fats Domino and the Mills Brothers. What do you remember about that?
And Freddie Martin. Is his name there?
Freddie Martin's not here.
Well, he was in it.
Well, maybe it's because this says 'Jazz in the Movies.'
Oh, I see. Yeah.
Maybe if you didn't play jazz you don't get mentioned.
Yeah.
Did you all work together or were you all doing separate things?

Well, no, like we -- the Mills Brothers and I did -- we accompanied the Mills Brothers. They worked it into the plot. And there was a little conversation, very little. We did a number and then we did a number with the Mills Brothers, and then that was it. And then Freddie Martin came in the studio, and strangely enough he used my band. In

fact, Will Cowan said, "Look, do you mind, can we use your band for all the rest of the picture?" I said, "What about the studio musicians?" He said, "That's all right, we can use them." And he used my band for the whole picture, which of course made the guys in the band deliriously happy, because they picked up a nice paycheck.
Gee. Well, see, that isn't even in here. That was '57. Harry James, did he work then with your band, or did he work before you? How did Harry James --

Well, I don't know, I wasn't there. I left. I don't know who he -- knowing Harry, I would say that Harry is very particular. He will not work with anybody but his own band. I imagine he brought his -- but he wasn't even there that day, when all the -- I think his part was shot on a different day.
